_comment: Technical data-handling inventory. This file does not publish or approve legal policy wording.
local_credentials: Reads the signed-in user's Claude and Codex credentials locally. Existing optional Claude login refresh may contact Anthropic or invoke the Claude CLI. Credentials are never included in usage relay responses or browser settings responses.
stored_usage: Stores usage windows, reset times, billing summary, timestamps and the configured source label in local usage history. Diagnostic logs record source failures without relay access keys.

optional_relay.transport: Authenticated HTTP on the user's trusted private LAN; HTTP is not encrypted. No automatic cloud upload or public port forwarding.
optional_relay.authentication: Separate relay access key, stored in a user-restricted token file on the host and local settings on the viewer. Browser settings responses omit secret values.
optional_relay.polling: One background usage poll every three minutes on the relay host. Viewers read the cached snapshot; failed polls invalidate it until recovery.
optional_relay.startup: Opt-in Windows task runs under the signed-in Claude user and restarts after process failure. Removing the task preserves local files.

lan_viewing: The existing optional phone/browser UI serves usage and source labels on the user's LAN.
codex_status: Desktop and optional LAN views receive the existing Codex state plus a typed local-credential or HTTP-access rejection reason, numeric HTTP error status and last/approximate next check times. These observations do not establish subscription expiry. No upstream error body, credential, credential-store path or account identifier is included. Refresh status rereads the local cached status/usage only; it adds no provider request or credential refresh.

openrouter_account_spend.source: Opt-in exporter makes read-only OpenRouter Analytics queries across all API keys accessible to the configured account management credential. Replaces the launcher-only card; no launcher totals are relabelled as account totals.
openrouter_account_spend.credentials: The management credential stays in its configured protected file on the exporting machine. Only aggregate summaries are copied to the viewer; no credential, raw account identifier, prompt, model response or individual request record is sent to browsers.
openrouter_account_spend.transport: Configurable local export or authenticated SSH from the viewer to an existing trusted exporter host. Queries send time ranges and metric/dimension names to OpenRouter, not prompts. No inference is performed.
openrouter_account_spend.storage: Stores one atomically replaced account spend summary on the exporter and in local application data on the viewer. Includes costs, request counts, model/provider labels, token totals, 31 daily totals, periods, freshness and an internal credential fingerprint to prevent mixed-account caches. Failures preserve matching-account last-good values with a stale flag.
openrouter_account_spend.sharing: Desktop and optional LAN browsers receive aggregate costs/counts, model/provider breakdowns, dates and stale/unavailable state via the existing local backend. The internal credential fingerprint is not included.
openrouter_account_spend.scheduling: Optional per-user task refreshes every five minutes with bounded runtime. App reads the summary every three minutes and does not contact OpenRouter directly.
openrouter_account_spend.deletion: Removing the optional sync task stops refreshes. Removing the exporter output and local application-data summary removes these cached spend totals; the existing usage-logs clear option does not remove this independent cache.

stats_history.source: Claude statistics read the existing local monthly usage logs. Codex statistics record quota windows from successful fresh results of the existing Codex poll; there are no additional provider requests.
stats_history.storage: Codex quota history is append-only monthly JSONL under the existing usage-log directory, separated by a SHA-256 account identifier. Records contain the observation time, quota-window durations, used percentages and reset times. They do not contain raw account IDs, credentials, credit balances, prompts or responses. History begins when this feature is installed and is retained until cleared with usage logs.
stats_history.derived: Statistics select a bounded 1-, 7- or 30-day period ending at the requested time, capped at the present. Curves accumulate observed positive percentage-point changes from a zero baseline. Missing readings and reset changes do not establish complete consumption.
stats_history.sharing: The existing desktop and optional LAN Stats page receive selected-period aggregate curves, window labels, time bounds and the earliest available observation. Account identifiers and raw persisted records are not returned.
stats_history.deletion: The existing Clear data usage-logs option and usage-log uninstall cleanup remove Codex quota history with the Claude usage logs.

codex_credits.source: Uses the existing authenticated Codex usage poll; adds no external API calls or prompt collection.
codex_credits.storage: Keeps at most eight days and 5000 timestamped credit-balance samples in the local usage-log/codex-credits.json file. A SHA-256 account identifier separates histories; raw account IDs and credentials are not saved in this file or sent to browsers.
codex_credits.derived: Calculates approximate observed balance decreases, 24-hour and seven-day spending rates, estimated days remaining and daily totals for today plus the previous six UTC dates. Today's total is day-to-date as of the last reading, not a full-day projection. Grants, corrections, missing observations and expiry can limit the estimates.
codex_credits.sharing: The existing desktop/LAN usage response includes credit balance, calculated estimates, daily totals and freshness; no new cloud upload.
codex_credits.deletion: The existing Clear data usage-logs option removes the credit history with the other usage logs.

dashboard_layout: Stores ordered card identifiers in local settings. The dedicated card-order endpoint shares the order with connected LAN browsers; no prompts, account IDs or credentials are included.
